findings.evidence: The product mocks are built from live HTML text with no role, accessible name or aria-hidden (dom-1440: name null, ariaHidden null). A screen reader reads them inline as page content: 'Tilly Invoices Clients Replies 2 Search invoices New invoice Invoices All Chasing Paid Outstanding £4,520.00 No. Client Due Amount Status 0045 Example Press...' (bodyText), roughly 250 words of mock UI, including fake control labels ('Search invoices', 'New invoice') that are not controls. Only the showcase has a figcaption.
findings.after: <figure class="slot app" role="img" aria-label="Tilly's invoice list: seven invoices, £4,520 outstanding, invoice 0042 to Example Kitchen being chased with reminder 2 due today"> with the inner .ui aria-hidden="true"; or keep it readable but add a <figcaption> naming it as a screen of the app
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content and 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: an illustration must be identified as one and summarised, not read as page controls.

findings.where: hero mock: 'Chasing' row date '2 Oct' (#bb3d31 on #f9e4de, 13px)
findings.evidence: Verified sweep A11-001: 4.49:1 against 4.5:1 required; real but marginal, and inside an illustration. The same red on the plain ground (30 Sep / 2 Oct in other mocks) passes.
findings.before: color: #bb3d31 on the salmon row tint
findings.after: Darken the late-date red one step (e.g. #a8352a) or lighten the row tint so the pair clears 4.5:1

findings.where: mock timelines: red due dates ('30 Sep' in #replies, '2 Oct' in hero and invoice)
findings.evidence: Lateness of a due date is shown by red alone in the replies thread ('Due 30 Sep' in red, no 'late' word); the hero row and invoice also carry a 'Chasing'/'Overdue' pill, so they pass, but the thread row relies on colour.
findings.after: Add a word or icon: '30 Sep, late' or a visually hidden ' (overdue)' span

strengths: Skip link first, landmarks complete (header, two navs, main, footer), lang en-GB, a descriptive title; h1 then one h2 per question section, each heading a real question that describes its section.
Every focus stop has a 2px solid outline in the accent colour, none covered by the header; tab order follows reading order (focus.json 0-12).
The signup field has a visible label 'Email address' and the button's name matches its visible text; the unconnected form says 'Nothing was sent: this form is not connected yet.'
Status badges carry words (Sent, Reply logged, Chasing, Paid, Overdue), not colour alone; links have specific names ('See a reminder', 'What clients get').
